title: Paris traffic, bicycles and an underground club with no elevator
summary: In Paris he marveled at the traffic and fearless cyclists and sat in at a club many flights underground, hard on his bad leg.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Were you moving so fast, Herman, that you never had time to stop in town and get to see much of it?
No -- yes -- I mean -- in Paris I liked to went out of my mind.
(Laughter.)
How long did you stay there?
Let me see, we were there a couple of days. Was it two, or three days? But what happened, coming through the city there, man, whew! I never saw so much traffic.
(Laughter.)
And bicycles! You see these old -- look like fifty, sixty, or seventy year old women, men, and they

sit on the bike (laughs). They didn't look around. They were ignoring the cars, and they didn't break their gait. And the cars were passing them, going and coming. I say I couldn't -- I say couldn't, anyway in the world I could drive here.
(Laughter.)
Somebody's going to get hit. I never saw anybody get hit. No.
Did you -- while you were two or three days in Paris did you sit in anywhere? You had one --
Yes. Yes.
You played one date there, but --

Yeah, yeah. It was -- let me think. You go in, you go all the way down three or four streets down, floors down, you're way down, down under the ground. Club -- it was the club, and we went down there and sat in and jammed, and you keep going down winding stair, winding stair, winding stairs, until you get -- I don't know how many flights down, floors down, in the ground.
I didn't like it. I mean --
You mean -- well, it was your leg, you mean.
Yeah, you know.
Going down all that.
You've got to walk, and there's no
such thing as an elevator, you know.
